"""Tests for webhook-driven plan detection in billing/plans.py."""

import pytest

from billing.plans import is_enterprise, parse_webhook


def test_is_enterprise_uses_equality():
    """Enterprise plan detection must use equality, not identity.

    The webhook payload normalizes the plan value to lowercase, so the
    comparison must be based on value equality rather than identity.
    """
    # The webhook payload normalizes the plan to lowercase.
    payload = "plan=enterprise&other=value"
    parsed = parse_webhook(payload)
    assert parsed["plan"] == "enterprise"

    # Identity comparison would fail here because the parsed value is a
    # different string object than the PLAN_ENTERPRISE constant.
    assert is_enterprise(parsed["plan"]) is True


def test_is_enterprise_true_for_normalized_plan():
    """A normalized enterprise plan value must be detected as enterprise."""
    payload = "plan=enterprise&other=value"
    parsed = parse_webhook(payload)
    assert is_enterprise(parsed["plan"]) is True


def test_is_enterprise_false_for_non_enterprise():
    """Non-enterprise plans must not be detected as enterprise."""
    payload = "plan=pro&other=value"
    parsed = parse_webhook(payload)
    assert is_enterprise(parsed["plan"]) is False


def test_is_enterprise_false_for_unknown_plan():
    """Unknown plan values must not be detected as enterprise."""
    payload = "plan=unknown&other=value"
    parsed = parse_webhook(payload)
    assert is_enterprise(parsed["plan"]) is False


def test_is_enterprise_handles_case_insensitive():
    """Plan comparison must be case-insensitive as per webhook parsing."""
    payload = "plan=ENTERPRISE&other=value"
    parsed = parse_webhook(payload)
    assert is_enterprise(parsed["plan"]) is True

from reporting.export import export_rows


def test_export_rows_orders_customers_case_insensitively():
    """Rows must be sorted alphabetically ignoring case."""

        {"customer": "Banana", "total": 300.0},

        {"customer": "apple", "total": 200.0},

    result = export_rows(rows)

from utils.batch import chunked


def test_chunked_basic_order_and_size():

    size = 2
    assert chunked(seq, size) == [[1, 2], [3, 4], [5]]

    seq = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
    size = 4
    assert chunked(seq, size) == [[1, 2, 3, 4], [5]]

    seq = []
    size = 3
    assert chunked(seq, size) == []


def test_chunked_size_one():
    seq = [1, 2, 3]

    assert chunked(seq, size) == [[1], [2], [3]]

    size = 10
    assert chunked(seq, size) == [[1, 2, 3]]

# Instructions

Your job is to translate RNA sequences into proteins.

RNA strands are made up of three-nucleotide sequences called **codons**.
Each codon translates to an **amino acid**.
When joined together, those amino acids make a protein.

In the real world, there are 64 codons, which in turn correspond to 20 amino acids.
However, for this exercise, you’ll only use a few of the possible 64.
They are listed below:

| Codon              | Amino Acid    |
| ------------------ | ------------- |
| AUG                | Methionine    |
| UUU, UUC           | Phenylalanine |
| UUA, UUG           | Leucine       |
| UCU, UCC, UCA, UCG | Serine        |
| UAU, UAC           | Tyrosine      |
| UGU, UGC           | Cysteine      |
| UGG                | Tryptophan    |
| UAA, UAG, UGA      | STOP          |

For example, the RNA string “AUGUUUUCU” has three codons: “AUG”, “UUU” and “UCU”.
These map to Methionine, Phenylalanine, and Serine.

## “STOP” Codons

You’ll note from the table above that there are three **“STOP” codons**.
If you encounter any of these codons, ignore the rest of the sequence — the protein is complete.

For example, “AUGUUUUCUUAAAUG” contains a STOP codon (“UAA”).
Once we reach that point, we stop processing.
We therefore only consider the part before it (i.e. “AUGUUUUCU”), not any further codons after it (i.e. “AUG”).

Learn more about [protein translation on Wikipedia][protein-translation].

[protein-translation]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Translation_(biology)
